newsitem.title: FRANCE: Euro-deputies criticise troop delays in Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Euro-deputies criticise troop delays in Zaire.

text.p: The European Parliament lashed out on Thursday at the international community's delay in sending troops to eastern Zaire to get aid to refugees.
It urged European Union leaders meeting in Dublin on Friday and Saturday to discuss the issue "as a matter of priority".

The assembly said it deplored the way divisions within the EU, U.S. reluctance to send soldiers and the unwillingness to cooperate of governments in the region were hindering the deployment of military protection for aid workers trying to reach hundreds of thousands of refugees.

"The stalemate in the situation in eastern Zaire is further proof of the lack of political will, both of members of the U.N. Security Council, which seems unable to take any operational steps, and of the EU, which lacks initiatives and a comprehensive approach," the parliament said in a resolution.
EU aid chief Emma Bonino earlier accused the West of indifference towards the "missing" refugees, who are cut off from all aid and endangered by fighting in the Kivu region.

"We're being told 'there's only about 200,000 people involved, lost in Kivu'. So there's a new criterion in humanitarian conventions whereby a tolerance threshold is now 200,000. Or is it 300,000 or 400,000?"
"That's what worries me. And it worries me that nobody's talking about it any more," Bonino told the 626-member assembly.
Bonino said the European Commission backed the Euro-deputies' call for the 14 countries who have promised troops to agree on action when they meet on Friday.
Aid agencies and the U.S. military estimate that up to 600,000 Hutu refugees have returned to Rwanda since November, but the whereabouts of some 700,000 others is a mystery.
